Definition: from G1223 and G4650; to dissipate, i.e. (genitive case) to rout or separate; specially, to winnow; figuratively, to squander:--disperse, scatter (abroad), strew, waste.
BiblicalUsage: To scatter is what happens when the shepherd is struck and the sheep are driven apart. Jesus quotes it on the night of His arrest, the prodigal scatters his inheritance in riotous living, and the disciples are scattered abroad after Stephen's death, preaching wherever they go.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe scattering is God's strange way of sowing. The sheep scattered at the cross, the money scattered in the far country, the church scattered by persecution — and every scattering spread the seed further than staying home ever would.
